concepts.name: Budget in Parliament: documents, cut motions, grants and the Finance Bill
concepts.description: Budget documents and the Economic Survey, the Railway Budget merger, cut motions and the guillotine, the Appropriation Bill, special grants, the Vote on Account, the Interim Budget and the Finance Bill.
concepts.idea: The budget passes through demands for grants (voted separately, cut motions, guillotine), an Appropriation Bill that bars amendments to voted and charged sums, and a Finance Bill that can be amended and must be passed within 75 days.
concepts.rule: The budget (Article 112 calls it the annual financial statement) is laid with documents such as the Expenditure Budget, Receipts Budget, Outcome Budget and FRBM statements; the Economic Survey is now presented before it, and the Railway Budget, separated in 1924 on the Acworth Committee report, was merged in 2017. Each demand is voted separately in the Lok Sabha, with policy (Re 1), economy and token (Rs 100) cut motions; on the last allotted day the guillotine puts all remaining demands to vote and an Appropriation Bill follows, with no amendment altering voted or charged sums. Supplementary, additional, excess (after PAC examination), exceptional grants, votes of credit and token grants meet special needs, and a Vote on Account (usually two months, one-sixth) bridges the gap before the Appropriation Act. The Finance Bill gives effect to taxation, can be amended, and must be enacted within 75 days (Provisional Collection of Taxes Act, 1931).
concepts.example: A member who wants to protest a grievance of a ministry moves a token cut motion of Rs 100; a member who disapproves its policy moves a policy cut reducing the demand to Re 1.

questions.q: Along with the budget speech, a set of statements is laid before Parliament because a fiscal-responsibility law requires it. Which one of the following is among the statements mandated under the Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management (FRBM) Act?
o: Revenue Buoyancy and Tax Elasticity Statement
questions.e: The FRBM statements listed with the budget documents are the Macro-Economic Framework Statement, the Fiscal Policy Strategy Statement and the Medium-Term Fiscal Policy Statement.
w: Not an FRBM statement; the Act's statements listed with the budget are the macro-economic, fiscal-policy-strategy and medium-term fiscal-policy statements.
Not an FRBM statement; no such growth-strategy statement is mandated by the Act.
Not an FRBM statement; devolution to States is dealt with through Finance Commission reports, not this Act.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Union Budget and the documents associated with it:

1. The Constitution itself uses the word 'Budget' for the annual statement of estimated receipts and expenditure, in Article 112.
2. The Demands for Grants are presented ministry-wise, and the Expenditure Budget, Receipts Budget and Budget at a Glance are among the documents laid.
3. The Outcome Budget links the expenditure to outputs and outcomes.
4. The Finance Bill is among the documents laid with the budget speech, whereas the Appropriation Bill is introduced only after the demands for grants have been voted.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: The Constitution nowhere uses the word 'budget'; Article 112 calls it the 'annual financial statement'. Statement 2 is correct: These are listed budget documents. Statement 3 is correct: That is its purpose. Statement 4 is correct: The Finance Bill figures in the list of budget documents and the Appropriation Bill follows the voting of demands. So the key is 2, 3 and 4 only.
w: '1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct:
'2 and 3 only' leaves out statement 4, which is correct:
'1, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct:

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Economic Survey:

1. It is now presented to Parliament one day or a few days before the Budget, whereas it earlier accompanied the Budget.
2. It is prepared by the Ministry of Finance and gives an analytical picture of the state of the economy, supplying data and context for budget proposals.
3. Article 112 requires the Economic Survey to be laid before both Houses every year along with the annual financial statement.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: the Economic Survey is now presented to Parliament a day or a few days before the Budget, whereas it earlier accompanied the Budget. Statement 2 is correct: it is prepared by the Ministry of Finance and gives an analytical picture of the state of the economy, supplying data and context for budget proposals. Statement 3 is incorrect: Article 112 requires only the annual financial statement to be laid; the Survey is not a constitutional document. So the key is 1 and 2 only.
w: '2 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect, and leaves out statement 1, which is correct.
'1 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct.
'1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect.

questions.q: India had a separate Railway Budget alongside the General Budget until it was merged in 2017. When was the Railway Budget separated from the General Budget, and on whose report?
questions.a: 1924, on the recommendations of the Acworth Committee
o: 1924, on the recommendations of the Acworth Committee
1921, on the recommendations of the Acworth Committee
1947, on the recommendations of the Constituent Assembly
2017, on the recommendations of the Bibek Debroy Committee
questions.e: The Acworth Committee reported in 1921 and the Railway Budget was separated in 1924.
w: 1921 is the year of the Acworth report; the separation itself came in 1924.
The Railway Budget was separated long before Independence; the Constituent Assembly did not recommend it.
2017 is the year of the merger, not of the separation of the Railway Budget.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Railway Budget:

1. Until 2017 the Government had two budgets, a Railway Budget for the Ministry of Railways and a General Budget for the other ministries.
2. Railways was then the largest commercial undertaking of the government, which was the justification for treating it separately.
3. After the 2017 merger the Ministry of Railways no longer submits Demands for Grants; its finances are examined only through the Economic Survey.
4. One reason given for the merger is that railways had become a provider of public service rather than a purely commercial entity.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Until 2017 the Government had two budgets, a Railway Budget for the Ministry of Railways and a General Budget for the other ministries. Statement 2 is correct: Railways was then the largest commercial undertaking of the government, which was the justification for treating it separately. Statement 3 is incorrect: Railway finances are scrutinised through the Demands for Grants of the Ministry of Railways within the Union Budget. Statement 4 is correct. So the key is 1, 2 and 4 only.
w: '1, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct:
'1 and 2 only' leaves out statement 4, which is correct:
'2 and 4 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct:

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the separation and merger of the Railway Budget:

1. One aim of the 1924 separation was to introduce flexibility in railway finance.
2. Another aim was to secure stability of general revenues by an assured annual contribution from railway revenues.
3. The 2017 merger of the Railway Budget with the General Budget was carried out on the recommendations of the Acworth Committee.
4. A supporting argument for the 2017 merger is that integration improves resource allocation, fiscal discipline and planning, and matches global norms where railways have no separate budget.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: one aim of the 1924 separation was to introduce flexibility in railway finance. Statement 2 is correct: Another aim was to secure stability of general revenues by an assured annual contribution from railway revenues. Statement 3 is incorrect: The Acworth Committee (report of 1921) led to the separation of 1924, not to the merger of 2017. Statement 4 is correct. So exactly 3 statement(s) are correct.
w: 'None' miscounts: exactly 3 statement(s) are correct.
'Only one' miscounts: exactly 3 statement(s) are correct.
'Only two' miscounts: exactly 3 statement(s) are correct.

questions.q:
Match the entries in List-I with the correct entries in List-II.

List-I
A. Policy cut motion
B. Economy cut motion
C. Token cut motion
D. Vote on Account

List-II
1. Proposes a specific reduction, either a lump sum or omission or reduction of an item, to show possible savings
2. Ventilates a specific grievance by proposing a nominal reduction of Rs 100
3. Disapproves the policy behind a demand and seeks to reduce it to Re 1
4. Temporary advance approval, usually for two months at about one-sixth of estimated expenditure
questions.e: A policy cut disapproves the policy and reduces the demand to Re 1 (3); an economy cut shows savings by a specific reduction (1); a token cut ventilates a grievance with Rs 100 (2); the Vote on Account is a temporary advance (4).
w: Policy and economy cuts are interchanged: the policy cut is the Re 1 disapproval of policy.
Economy and token cuts are interchanged: the token cut is the Rs 100 grievance motion.
Policy and token cuts are interchanged: the token cut carries the Rs 100 reduction, not Re 1.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about how the Lok Sabha votes on the demands for grants:

1. Each demand for grant is taken up and voted separately, and members may move cut motions to reduce it.
2. A policy cut motion seeks to reduce a demand by Rs 100 and the mover must not suggest any alternative policy.
3. A token cut motion ventilates a specific grievance and proposes a reduction of Rs 100.
4. An economy cut motion points to possible savings and proposes either a lump-sum reduction or the omission or reduction of an item.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Each demand for grant is taken up and voted separately, and members may move cut motions to reduce it. Statement 2 is incorrect: A policy cut seeks to reduce the demand to Re 1 and the mover may advocate an alternative policy. Statement 3 is correct: A token cut motion ventilates a specific grievance and proposes a reduction of Rs 100. Statement 4 is correct. So the key is 1, 3 and 4 only.
w: '1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct:
'1 and 3 only' leaves out statement 4, which is correct:
'1 and 4 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct:

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: Since 2017 the finances of the railways are scrutinised through the Demands for Grants of the Ministry of Railways within the Union Budget.
Statement-II: In 2017 the Railway Budget was merged with the General Budget.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct: railway finances are now discussed within the Union Budget. Statement-II is correct: the merger took place in 2017. The merger is exactly why railway finances are now scrutinised inside the Union Budget, so Statement-II explains Statement-I.
w: Statement-II does supply the reason for Statement-I, so it does explain it.
Statement-II is correct, so it cannot be called incorrect.
Statement-I is correct, so it cannot be called incorrect.

questions.q: On the last day allotted for the demands for grants, the Speaker puts all the remaining demands to the vote of the House whether or not they have been discussed. This procedural device is known as
questions.e: Putting all remaining demands to the vote on the last allotted day, discussed or not, is the guillotine.
w: Kangaroo closure skips intervening clauses of a Bill while taking up important clauses for debate.
Closure by compartments groups the clauses of a Bill into parts before debate.
Simple closure is a motion that the matter has been sufficiently discussed and be now put to the vote.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Appropriation Bill:

1. Article 114 bars any withdrawal from the Consolidated Fund of India unless Parliament has authorised it through an Appropriation law.
2. The Appropriation Bill provides only for the grants voted by the Lok Sabha; the expenditure charged on the Consolidated Fund is left out of it.
3. No amendment may be proposed to it that would vary the amount or alter the destination of a voted grant or of charged expenditure.
4. With the President's assent it becomes the Appropriation Act, without which even approved expenditure cannot legally be spent.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Article 114 bars any withdrawal from the Consolidated Fund of India unless Parliament has authorised it through an Appropriation law.. Statement 2 is incorrect: It covers both the voted grants and the charged expenditure. Statement 3 is correct: No amendment may be proposed to it that would vary the amount or alter the destination of a voted grant or of charged expenditure.. Statement 4 is correct. So the key is 1, 3 and 4 only.
w: '1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct:
'1, 2 and 4 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct:
'1 and 3 only' leaves out statement 4, which is correct:

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the passing of demands for grants and the Appropriation Bill:

1. After all demands are voted, individually or through the guillotine, they are consolidated into an Appropriation Bill.
2. Demands not reached by the last allotted day are dropped from the Appropriation Bill.
3. Amendments that change the amount of a voted grant are not allowed to the Appropriation Bill.
4. It is the Finance Minister, not the Speaker, who puts the remaining demands to the vote on the last allotted day.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: After all demands are voted, individually or through the guillotine, they are consolidated into an Appropriation Bill. Statement 2 is incorrect: Under the guillotine they are put to the vote together and deemed approved. Statement 3 is correct: Amendments that change the amount of a voted grant are not allowed to the Appropriation Bill. Statement 4 is incorrect: The Speaker puts all remaining demands to the vote. So exactly 2 statement(s) are correct.
w: 'None' miscounts: exactly 2 statement(s) are correct.
'Only one' miscounts: exactly 2 statement(s) are correct.
'Only three' miscounts: exactly 2 statement(s) are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about grants made by Parliament in addition to the regular budget:

1. A supplementary grant is given when the amount authorised for a service in the year proves insufficient.
2. An additional grant is given for a new service not contemplated when the budget was prepared.
3. An excess grant covers expenditure above the amount authorised and is voted after the financial year.
4. An excess grant is put to the Lok Sabha directly, without any examination by the Public Accounts Committee.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct:(Article 115). Statement 2 is correct: An additional grant is given for a new service not contemplated when the budget was prepared. Statement 3 is correct: An excess grant covers expenditure above the amount authorised and is voted after the financial year. Statement 4 is incorrect: The PAC must examine it first, and then the Lok Sabha approves. So the key is 1, 2 and 3 only.
w: '1, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct:
'1 and 3 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct:
'1, 2 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct:

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about vote of credit, exceptional grant and token grant:

1. A vote of credit is for unforeseen, urgent expenditure whose amount cannot be stated with the usual details because of the magnitude or indefinite character of the service.
2. An exceptional grant is for a special purpose and forms no part of the current services of a financial year.
3. A token grant is made when funds for a new service can be found by reappropriation, so a token sum is voted and no additional expenditure arises.
4. Supplementary, additional, excess and exceptional grants and the vote of credit are passed by a procedure quite different from that of the regular budget.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct:(Article 116). Statement 2 is correct:(Article 116). Statement 3 is correct: A token grant is made when funds for a new service can be found by reappropriation, so a token sum is voted and no additional expenditure arises. Statement 4 is incorrect: They are regulated by the same procedure that applies to the regular budget. So the key is 1, 2 and 3 only.
w: '1, 2 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct:
'1 and 3 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct:
'2 and 3 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct:

questions.q: Parliament sometimes sanctions money for spending that has already taken place beyond the original authorisation. Which one of the following grants must be examined by the Public Accounts Committee before the demand is submitted to the Lok Sabha for voting?
questions.e: Only the excess grant, covering money spent beyond the authorised amount and voted after the financial year, goes through the PAC first.
w: An additional grant is for a new service and carries no PAC step.
A vote of credit is a blank cheque for unforeseen demand and carries no PAC step.
An exceptional grant is for a special purpose outside current services and carries no PAC step.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: A vote of credit leaves the Executive free to spend as needs arise, much like a blank cheque signed by the Lok Sabha.
Statement-II: A vote of credit must be examined by the Public Accounts Committee before the demand is submitted to the Lok Sabha for voting.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
o: Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct: the vote of credit is a grant for an unexpected demand whose amount cannot be stated with the usual details, so it is called a blank cheque given to the Executive. Statement-II is incorrect: it is the excess grant, not the vote of credit, that the Public Accounts Committee examines before the demand goes to the Lok Sabha.
w: Statement-II is untrue, so it cannot be a reason for Statement-I.
Statement-II is untrue, so the two cannot both be correct.
Statement-I is correct: the vote of credit is the blank-cheque grant.
tr: Which grant goes to the PAC

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Vote on Account and the Interim Budget:

1. A Vote on Account is passed before the general discussion on the budget begins.
2. The financial year begins on 1 April, and since the budget process may not finish by then the Lok Sabha may grant a Vote on Account.
3. It is usually valid for two months and typically equals one-sixth of the total estimated expenditure.
4. In an election year the Vote on Account may be taken for a longer period, about three to five months.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: It is passed after the general discussion on the budget is over. Statement 2 is correct: The financial year begins on 1 April, and since the budget process may not finish by then the Lok Sabha may grant a Vote on Account. Statement 3 is correct: It is usually valid for two months and typically equals one-sixth of the total estimated expenditure. Statement 4 is correct:(the Constitution itself fixes no period). So the key is 2, 3 and 4 only.
w: '1, 2 and 4 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct:
'2 and 4 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct:
'2 and 3 only' leaves out statement 4, which is correct:

questions.q: Under the Provisional Collection of Taxes Act, 1931, the Finance Bill giving effect to the tax proposals of the Union Budget has to be enacted within a fixed period. Which one of the following is that period?
questions.e: The Finance Bill must be passed by Parliament and assented to by the President within 75 days.
w: 60 days is not the period fixed by the 1931 Act.
90 days is not the period fixed by the 1931 Act.
45 days is not the period fixed by the 1931 Act.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Finance Bill:

1. It gives legal effect to the tax proposals of the budget, while the Appropriation Bill authorises the expenditure.
2. It cannot be introduced in the Rajya Sabha and needs the recommendation of the President; it is subject to all the conditions applicable to a Money Bill.
3. Unlike the Appropriation Bill, it can be amended, for example to reduce a tax rate or to reject a specific tax provision.
4. The debate on it is wide-ranging and can cover tax policy, economic and monetary policy, public administration and grievances within Union jurisdiction.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: the Finance Bill gives legal effect to the tax proposals of the budget, while the Appropriation Bill authorises the expenditure. Statement 2 is correct: like a Money Bill, it can be introduced only in the Lok Sabha on the recommendation of the President. Statement 3 is correct: unlike the Appropriation Bill, it can be amended, for example to reduce a tax rate or to reject a specific tax provision. Statement 4 is correct: the debate on it is wide-ranging and covers the general administration of the Union. So exactly 4 statements are correct.
w: 'Only one' miscounts: exactly 4 statements are correct.
'Only three' miscounts: exactly 4 statements are correct.
'None' miscounts: exactly 4 statements are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the completion of the budget process:

1. The Finance Act legalises the income side of the budget and completes the process of enactment of the budget.
2. An Interim Budget is presented in the year of a general election and the regular budget is presented after the new government assumes office.
3. Expenditure such as the salaries, allowances and pensions of Supreme Court judges is charged on the Consolidated Fund, so it can only be discussed and not voted upon.
4. Debt charges of the Government of India, and sums needed to satisfy a court judgement or decree, are also expenditure charged on the Consolidated Fund.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: The Finance Act legalises the income side of the budget and completes the process of enactment of the budget. Statement 2 is correct: An Interim Budget is presented in the year of a general election and the regular budget is presented after the new government assumes office. Statement 3 is correct: Expenditure such as the salaries, allowances and pensions of Supreme Court judges is charged on the Consolidated Fund, so it can only be discussed and not voted upon. Statement 4 is correct. So the key is 1, 2, 3 and 4.
w: '1, 2 and 4 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct:
'1, 2 and 3 only' leaves out statement 4, which is correct:
'1, 3 and 4 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct:

concepts.name: Legislative, executive, financial and constituent powers of Parliament
concepts.description: Union, State and Concurrent List powers, Ordinances, delegated legislation, control over the Executive, financial control and the three modes of amendment.
concepts.idea: Parliament legislates on the Union and Concurrent Lists, on State List subjects in five abnormal situations, controls the Executive through devices and committees, and amends the Constitution by simple, special or special-plus-ratification majority.
concepts.rule: According to Laxmikanth the Union List has 98 subjects, the Concurrent List 52 and the State List 59, and Parliament can legislate on State List subjects on a Rajya Sabha resolution, in a National Emergency, on request of two or more States, to implement treaties, and during President's Rule. An Ordinance under Article 123 lapses if not approved within six weeks of reassembly. The Executive frames subordinate legislation, watched by the Committee on Subordinate Legislation. The Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha, which shows lack of confidence by rejecting the Motion of Thanks or a Money Bill, or passing a censure, adjournment or cut motion. Parliament amends the Constitution by simple majority, special majority, or special majority with ratification by at least half the States, within the basic structure; only Parliament initiates an amendment.
concepts.example: If the Rajya Sabha passes a national-interest resolution, Parliament may make a law on a State List subject.

questions.q: Parliament has exclusive power to make laws on the Union List and on residuary subjects. As commonly counted, how many subjects does the Union List contain at present?
questions.e: The Union List has 98 subjects at present, against 97 originally.
w: 97 is the original number of subjects, not the present one.
99 does not match the commonly cited figure.
102 does not match the commonly cited figure.

questions.q: A law passed by Parliament and a law passed by a State Legislature on the same Concurrent List subject conflict with each other. As a general rule stated in the chapter (Article 254), which one of the following is correct?
questions.a: The law made by Parliament prevails over the State law
o: The law made by Parliament prevails over the State law
The State law prevails, because the subject lies in a shared list
The law passed later in time prevails whichever body made it
Both laws are suspended until the Supreme Court decides between them
questions.e: On Concurrent List subjects the law of Parliament prevails over the State law in case of conflict, subject to the exception in Article 254 for a State law that has received presidential assent.
w: Parliament has overriding power on this list, so the State law does not prevail as a rule.
The chapter does not say that the later law prevails regardless of who made it.
The Constitution does not suspend both laws pending a Supreme Court decision.

questions.q: The President promulgates an Ordinance under Article 123 while Parliament is in recess. If Parliament takes no action on it, the Ordinance ceases to operate on the expiry of
questions.a: six weeks from the reassembly of Parliament
o: six weeks from the reassembly of Parliament
six months from the date of promulgation
six weeks from the date of promulgation
fourteen days from the reassembly of Parliament
questions.e: An Ordinance must be approved by Parliament within six weeks of its reassembly, failing which it lapses.
w: Six months is the maximum gap between two sessions, not the life of an Ordinance counted from promulgation.
The six weeks run from reassembly, not from promulgation.
Fourteen days is the time the Rajya Sabha has for a Money Bill, not for an Ordinance.

questions.q: Under Article 368, a Constitution Amendment Bill needs a 'special majority' in each House. Which one of the following correctly describes it?
questions.a: A majority of the total membership of the House plus at least two-thirds of the members present and voting
o: A majority of the total membership of the House plus at least two-thirds of the members present and voting
Two-thirds of the total membership of the House, without any further condition on the members who are present and voting
A simple majority of the members present and voting in each House, followed by a joint sitting of both Houses
Two-thirds of the members present and voting in the Lok Sabha alone, with no vote in the Rajya Sabha
questions.e: The special majority is a majority of the total membership of each House together with at least two-thirds of the members present and voting.
w: Two-thirds of total membership is the rule for impeaching the President, not for Article 368.
A simple majority with a joint sitting is the ordinary-Bill route, not the amendment route.
Each House must pass the Bill; the Lok Sabha alone cannot do it.

questions.q: Only Parliament can initiate the process of amending the Constitution; a State Legislature cannot. In which one of the following matters does a resolution of a State Legislature set in motion action by Parliament?
questions.a: Creation or abolition of the Legislative Council of that State
o: Creation or abolition of the Legislative Council of that State
Alteration of the boundaries of that State
Creation of an All-India Service common to the Centre and the States
questions.e: The one exception is a State Legislature's resolution asking Parliament to create or abolish its Legislative Council, on which Parliament legislates.
w: Alteration of State boundaries is initiated by Parliament and the views of the State are only referred to; it is not the exception named in the chapter.
Article 368 can be amended only by the Parliament route with ratification, never on a State's initiative.
An All-India Service is created on a Rajya Sabha resolution (Article 312), not a State Legislature resolution.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the legislative lists of the Seventh Schedule:

1. The Union List began with 97 entries when the Constitution came into force.
2. The State List began with 66 entries when the Constitution came into force.
3. The Concurrent List now carries 52 entries, up from the 47 with which it began.
4. Residuary subjects, those not enumerated in any of the three lists, belong to the State Legislatures.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: the Union List had 97 entries originally. Statement 2 is correct: the State List began with 66 entries. Statement 3 is correct: the Concurrent List began with 47 entries and now carries 52 after additions by amendments. Statement 4 is incorrect: under Article 248 Parliament has exclusive power over residuary subjects. So the key is 1, 2 and 3 only.
w: '1, 2 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect, and leaves out statement 3, which is correct.
'2 and 3 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct.
'2, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect, and leaves out statement 1, which is correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following situations:

1. The Rajya Sabha passes a resolution that Parliament should legislate on a State List subject in the national interest.
2. The Lok Sabha passes a resolution that Parliament should legislate on a State List subject in the national interest.
3. President's Rule is in operation in the State concerned.
4. Legislation is needed to give effect to an international treaty, agreement or convention.

In which of the situations given above can Parliament make a law on a subject in the State List?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: The Rajya Sabha passes a resolution that Parliament should legislate on a State List subject in the national interest. Statement 2 is incorrect: The enabling resolution is that of the Rajya Sabha, not the Lok Sabha. Statement 3 is correct: President's Rule is in operation in the State concerned. Statement 4 is correct. So the key is 1, 3 and 4 only.
w: '2, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct:
'1, 2, 3 and 4' includes statement 2, which is incorrect:
'3 and 4 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct:

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Ordinance-making power of the President:

1. The President may promulgate an Ordinance under Article 123 even while both Houses are in session if the matter is urgent.
2. An Ordinance carries the authority of an Act of Parliament, yet it is only a stopgap law.
3. It must be approved by Parliament within six weeks of reassembly, otherwise it lapses.
4. If both Houses pass a resolution disapproving it, the Ordinance ceases to operate.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

concepts.name: Judicial and electoral powers, parliamentary privileges, breach and contempt
concepts.description: Parliament's judicial, electoral and other powers, the meaning and classification of privileges, collective and individual privileges, breach of privilege versus contempt, and the articles on privileges.
concepts.idea: Privileges are rights of Houses, committees and members, collective (publishing, excluding strangers, punishing) or individual (arrest immunity of 40 days in civil cases, speech immunity), and contempt is wider than breach of privilege.
concepts.rule: Parliament impeaches the President, removes the Vice-President by a Rajya Sabha resolution agreed to by the Lok Sabha, recommends removal of judges and the CAG, and takes part in elections. Privileges under Article 105 belong to the Houses, committees, members and persons entitled to speak, such as the Attorney General, but not the President. Collective privileges include publishing proceedings, excluding strangers, making rules (Article 118), punishing members and outsiders and barring legal process in the precincts without the presiding officer's permission. Individual privileges include freedom of speech, immunity from liability for speech and vote, and freedom from civil arrest for 40 days before and after a session. Breach of privilege is always contempt, but contempt is wider. Articles 105, 122, 194 and 212 are the key provisions.
concepts.example: A member cannot be sued for a speech in the House, but publishing a false report of the proceedings may be treated as contempt.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Threatening violence against a member of the House can amount to a breach of privilege or contempt. Statement 2 is correct: Publishing false or distorted reports of the proceedings can amount to contempt. Statement 3 is correct: Speeches or publications casting reflections on the House, its members or its committees can amount to contempt. Statement 4 is incorrect: No legal proceedings lie for publications made under Parliament's authority. So exactly 3 statement(s) are correct.
w: 'Only one' miscounts: exactly 3 statement(s) are correct.
'Only two' miscounts: exactly 3 statement(s) are correct.
'None' miscounts: exactly 3 statement(s) are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the sources and extent of parliamentary privileges:

1. Parliament has not so far made a special law codifying all its privileges.
2. Parliamentary privileges cover the President, since the Constitution makes him a part of Parliament.
3. The 44th Amendment Act replaced the privileges by a detailed statutory code.
4. Until Parliament defines them by law, the privileges are those of the United States Congress.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Parliament has not so far made a special law codifying all its privileges. Statement 2 is incorrect: The privileges do not extend to the President. Statement 3 is incorrect: It only dropped the direct reference to the British House of Commons, without changing the position. Statement 4 is incorrect: In the original text they were those of the British House of Commons, later reworded by the 44th Amendment. So exactly 1 statement(s) are correct.
w: 'None' miscounts: exactly 1 statement(s) are correct.
'Only two' miscounts: exactly 1 statement(s) are correct.
'Only three' miscounts: exactly 1 statement(s) are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: A member of the Lok Sabha cannot be sued in a court for anything said in a debate in the House.
Statement-II: A member's freedom of speech in the House is subject to the rules of procedure of the House.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct: no member is liable in any court for anything said in Parliament. Statement-II is correct: the freedom is subject to the Constitution and the rules. The rules limit what a member may say but do not give the reason for the immunity from court liability, so Statement-II does not explain Statement-I.
w: Both are correct but Statement-II is a separate fact, not the reason for Statement-I.
Statement-II is correct, so it cannot be called incorrect.
Statement-I is correct, so it cannot be called incorrect.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: A House of Parliament can punish an outsider found guilty of contempt by suspending or expelling him.
Statement-II: For members, the sanctions of a House include suspension and expulsion in addition to admonition, reprimand and imprisonment.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
o: Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
questions.e: Statement-I is incorrect: suspension and expulsion apply to members; for outsiders the sanctions are reprimand, admonition or imprisonment. Statement-II is correct: members face suspension and expulsion as well.
w: Statement-I is untrue, so the pair cannot be both correct.
Statement-I is untrue, so the pair cannot be both correct.
Statement-II is correct: members can be suspended or expelled.

questions.q:
Match the entries in List-I with the correct entries in List-II.

List-I
A. Breach of privilege
B. Contempt of the House
C. A collective privilege
D. An individual privilege

List-II
1. An act that obstructs the House or lowers its dignity even where no specific privilege is violated
2. The right to exclude strangers and hold secret sittings
3. Immunity from liability in any court for anything said or any vote given in Parliament
4. A direct violation of a specific right, privilege or immunity of a member or of the House
questions.e: Breach of privilege is a direct violation of a specific privilege (4); contempt is the wider obstruction or lowering of dignity (1); excluding strangers is a collective privilege (2); immunity for speech and vote in Parliament belongs to the individual member (3).
w: Breach and contempt are interchanged.
Collective and individual privileges are interchanged.
Breach and collective privilege are wrongly paired.

concepts.name: Parliamentary committees and the Rajya Sabha compared with the Lok Sabha
concepts.description: Why Parliament works through committees, the financial committees, the composition and election of the two Houses, Money Bill procedure, responsibility of the ministry and sessions.
concepts.idea: The Rajya Sabha is a permanent, indirectly elected House of at most 250 members with limited powers on Money Bills and no say in removing the ministry, while the Lok Sabha (at most 550) is directly elected and dissolvable.
concepts.rule: Committees help Parliament because it has little time and expertise. The Rajya Sabha has at most 250 members (238 elected, 12 nominated), is never dissolved, with one-third retiring every two years, and is elected through proportional representation by single transferable vote; the Lok Sabha (maximum 550, 543 at present according to Laxmikanth) is directly elected by first-past-the-post, and the nomination of Anglo-Indian members ended with the 104th Amendment (2019). A Money Bill is introduced only in the Lok Sabha, the Speaker's decision on its character is final under Article 110(3), and the Rajya Sabha must return it within 14 days; a no-confidence motion lies only in the Lok Sabha. Sessions are summoned by the President with a gap of at most six months.
concepts.example: A Money Bill that the Rajya Sabha holds beyond 14 days is deemed passed in the form the Lok Sabha passed it.

questions.q: The maximum strength of the Rajya Sabha is 250. Of these, how many are the representatives of the States and Union Territories, elected indirectly?
questions.e: The maximum strength is 250, of which 238 are elected representatives of States and Union Territories and 12 are nominated by the President.
w: 245 is the present total strength according to the chapter, including the 12 nominated members.
225 is the chapter's present figure for States only, not the 238 permitted for States and Union Territories.
233 does not match the chapter's figure.

questions.q: A Money Bill passed by the Lok Sabha is transmitted to the Rajya Sabha. Within how many days must the Rajya Sabha return it to the Lok Sabha, with or without recommendations?
questions.e: The Rajya Sabha can only make recommendations and must return the Money Bill within 14 days; if it does not, the Bill is deemed passed as the Lok Sabha passed it.
w: 7 days is not the period allowed to the Rajya Sabha.
30 days is not the period allowed to the Rajya Sabha.
Six months is the period after which a deadlock on an ordinary Bill is deemed to have occurred.

questions.q: The President summons each House of Parliament to meet from time to time. What is the longest permissible gap between two sessions of Parliament?
questions.e: The gap between two sessions cannot exceed six months, so Parliament meets at least twice a year.
w: Three months is not the constitutional limit.
Four months is not the constitutional limit.
A year would allow Parliament to meet only once a year, which the six-month rule prevents.

questions.q: Before 2020 the President nominated two members of the Anglo-Indian community to the Lok Sabha. The provision was allowed to lapse, with effect from 25 January 2020, by the
questions.e: The 104th Amendment Act, 2019 did not extend the Anglo-Indian nomination further, and the provision ceased to have effect on 25 January 2020.
w: The 95th Amendment, 2009 extended the provision up to 2020.
The 84th Amendment, 2001 froze the allocation of seats to the States.
The 61st Amendment, 1988 lowered the voting age from 21 to 18.

questions.q: If a question arises whether a Bill is a Money Bill, whose decision is final under Article 110(3) of the Constitution?
questions.a: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha, whose decision is final
o: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha, whose decision is final
The Chairman of the Rajya Sabha, acting on the advice of the Council of Ministers
The President of India, on the advice of the Attorney General
The Finance Minister, who introduces the Bill in the Lok Sabha
questions.e: The Speaker certifies a Bill as a Money Bill and his or her decision is final.
w: The Chairman of the Rajya Sabha does not decide this; the Bill reaches the Rajya Sabha with the Speaker's endorsement.
The President does not decide the category; he acts on the Speaker's certificate.
The Finance Minister only introduces the Bill; he or she does not decide its category.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Rajya Sabha:

1. It is a permanent House that is not subject to dissolution.
2. In contrast, the Lok Sabha is subject to dissolution and has a normal term of five years.
3. One-half of its members retire every two years.
4. Twelve seats are filled by Presidential nomination of persons drawn from art, literature, science and social service.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: It is a permanent House that is not subject to dissolution. Statement 2 is correct: In contrast, the Lok Sabha is subject to dissolution and has a normal term of five years. Statement 3 is incorrect: One-third of the members retire every two years. Statement 4 is correct. So the key is 1, 2 and 4 only.
w: '2, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct:
'1 and 2 only' leaves out statement 4, which is correct:
'1 and 4 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct:

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the manner of election to the two Houses:

1. In the Lok Sabha election a candidate must secure an absolute majority of the votes polled to be declared elected.
2. The representatives of the States in the Rajya Sabha are elected by the elected members of the State Legislative Assemblies by proportional representation with the single transferable vote.
3. The Lok Sabha is elected directly by the people from territorial constituencies, with the first-past-the-post system.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: The Lok Sabha uses the first-past-the-post system, in which the candidate who secures the most votes wins. Statement 2 is correct: The representatives of the States in the Rajya Sabha are elected by the elected members of the State Legislative Assemblies by proportional representation with the single transferable vote. Statement 3 is correct. So the key is 2 and 3 only.
w: '1 and 2 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct:
'2 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct:
'1 and 3 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct:

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the procedure for a Money Bill:

1. It can be introduced only in the Lok Sabha and not in the Rajya Sabha.
2. The Rajya Sabha can reject it by a majority, in which case a joint sitting of the two Houses is summoned.
3. The Lok Sabha may accept or reject all or any of the Rajya Sabha's recommendations, and the Bill is deemed passed by both Houses in either case.
4. If the Rajya Sabha does not return it within 14 days, it is deemed passed in the form originally passed by the Lok Sabha.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: It can be introduced only in the Lok Sabha and not in the Rajya Sabha. Statement 2 is incorrect: The Rajya Sabha cannot reject or amend it, and there is no provision of joint sitting for it. Statement 3 is correct. Statement 4 is correct. So the key is 1, 3 and 4 only.
w: '1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct:
'1 and 3 only' leaves out statement 4, which is correct:
'2, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct:

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the certification and introduction of a Money Bill:

1. The Chairman of the Rajya Sabha decides whether a Bill sent to the Rajya Sabha is a Money Bill.
2. A Money Bill carries the Speaker's endorsement as such when it goes to the Rajya Sabha and again when it is presented to the President.
3. A Money Bill is a Government Bill: only a Minister may move it, and only with the President's recommendation.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha decides. Statement 2 is correct: A Money Bill carries the Speaker's endorsement as such when it goes to the Rajya Sabha and again when it is presented to the President. Statement 3 is correct. So the key is 2 and 3 only.
w: '1 and 2 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct:
'2 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct:
'1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect:

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Rajya Sabha and the Council of Ministers:

1. A no-confidence motion cannot be moved in the Rajya Sabha; it can be moved only in the Lok Sabha.
2. The Council of Ministers is collectively responsible only to the Lok Sabha, as Article 75(3) provides.
3. Ministers, including the Prime Minister, can be members of either House but are responsible only to the Lok Sabha.
4. The Rajya Sabha can nevertheless discuss and criticise the policies and activities of the government.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: A no-confidence motion cannot be moved in the Rajya Sabha; it can be moved only in the Lok Sabha. Statement 2 is correct: The Council of Ministers is collectively responsible only to the Lok Sabha, as Article 75(3) provides. Statement 3 is correct: Ministers, including the Prime Minister, can be members of either House but are responsible only to the Lok Sabha. Statement 4 is correct. So the key is 1, 2, 3 and 4.
w: '1, 2 and 4 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct:
'2, 3 and 4 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct:
'1, 3 and 4 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct:

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the sessions of Parliament:

1. The President summons each House to meet at such time and place as he or she thinks fit.
2. The gap between two sessions may extend up to one year if the President so decides.
3. There are usually three sessions in a year: the Budget Session, the Monsoon Session and the Winter Session.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: The President summons each House to meet at such time and place as he or she thinks fit. Statement 2 is incorrect: The gap cannot exceed six months. Statement 3 is correct. So the key is 1 and 3 only.
w: '2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct:
'1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect:
'1 and 2 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct:

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the composition of the Houses:

1. The maximum strength of the Lok Sabha is 550: 530 representatives of the States and 20 of the Union Territories.
2. Before the 104th Amendment the Constitution envisaged a maximum of 552 Lok Sabha members, counting two Anglo-Indians nominated by the President.
3. The nomination of Anglo-Indians to the Lok Sabha was discontinued by the 95th Amendment Act, 2009.
4. The maximum strength of the Rajya Sabha is 250: 238 elected and 12 nominated by the President.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: The maximum strength of the Lok Sabha is 550: 530 representatives of the States and 20 of the Union Territories. Statement 2 is correct: 550 plus two nominated Anglo-Indians made 552. Statement 3 is incorrect: The 95th Amendment extended it to 2020; the 104th Amendment Act, 2019 discontinued it. Statement 4 is correct. So the key is 1, 2 and 4 only.
w: '2, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct:
'1 and 2 only' leaves out statement 4, which is correct:
'1, 2, 3 and 4' includes statement 3, which is incorrect:

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the special powers of the Rajya Sabha:

1. If a National Emergency, President's Rule or Financial Emergency is proclaimed while the Lok Sabha stands dissolved, the proclamation can remain effective on approval by the Rajya Sabha alone.
2. The creation of a new All-India Service common to the Union and the States is enabled by a Rajya Sabha resolution (Article 312).
3. Either House may begin the process of removing the Vice-President from office.
4. Only the Rajya Sabha can pass a resolution disapproving the continuance of a National Emergency.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: the proclamation stays effective on Rajya Sabha approval alone. Statement 2 is correct: Article 312. Statement 3 is incorrect: the removal resolution can be introduced only in the Rajya Sabha. Statement 4 is incorrect: a resolution for the discontinuance of a National Emergency can be passed only by the Lok Sabha. So the key is 1 and 2 only.
w: '2 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct:
'1 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct:
'1 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct:

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about parliamentary committees:

1. Parliament is assisted by committees because it neither has adequate time nor the expertise to scrutinise all measures in detail.
2. Standing committees are temporary and are wound up once their task is completed, while ad hoc committees are permanent.
3. Standing committees are permanent, constituted every year or periodically, and work on a continuous basis.
4. The Constitution mentions committees at various places but leaves their composition, tenure and functions to the rules of the two Houses.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Parliament is assisted by committees because it neither has adequate time nor the expertise to scrutinise all measures in detail. Statement 2 is incorrect: It is the reverse: standing committees are permanent and ad hoc committees are temporary. Statement 3 is correct: Standing committees are permanent, constituted every year or periodically, and work on a continuous basis. Statement 4 is correct. So the key is 1, 3 and 4 only.
w: '2, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct:
'1, 2 and 4 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct:
'1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct:

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the financial committees of Parliament:

1. Of the 22 members of the Public Accounts Committee, 15 come from the Lok Sabha and 7 from the Rajya Sabha.
2. The Estimates Committee consists of 30 members, all from the Lok Sabha.
3. The Committee on Public Undertakings consists of members of the Lok Sabha only.
4. Since 1967 the chairman of the Public Accounts Committee has been selected from the ruling party.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is correct. Statement 3 is incorrect: It has 22 members, 15 from the Lok Sabha and 7 from the Rajya Sabha. Statement 4 is incorrect: By convention since 1967 the chairman has been from the Opposition. So exactly 2 statement(s) are correct.
w: 'Only one' miscounts: exactly 2 statement(s) are correct.
'Only three' miscounts: exactly 2 statement(s) are correct.
'All four' miscounts: exactly 2 statement(s) are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the equality of the two Houses of Parliament:

1. The Rajya Sabha has equal powers with the Lok Sabha in the introduction and passage of ordinary Bills.
2. The Rajya Sabha can only discuss the budget and cannot vote on the demands for grants.
3. The Rajya Sabha has equal powers in financial Bills involving expenditure from the Consolidated Fund of India.
4. The Chairman of the Rajya Sabha presides over a joint sitting of the two Houses.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is correct. Statement 3 is correct. Statement 4 is incorrect: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha presides over a joint sitting. So exactly 3 statement(s) are correct.
w: 'None' miscounts: exactly 3 statement(s) are correct.
'Only two' miscounts: exactly 3 statement(s) are correct.
'All four' miscounts: exactly 3 statement(s) are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the composition of the Rajya Sabha:

1. Seats are allotted to the States on the basis of population, so the number of representatives varies from State to State.
2. The representatives of a Union Territory are directly elected by the people of that Territory.
3. All eight Union Territories have representation in the Rajya Sabha.
4. The Fourth Schedule governs how the seats of the Lok Sabha are shared among the States and Union Territories.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect: They are indirectly elected by an electoral college specially constituted for the purpose. Statement 3 is incorrect: Only three (Delhi, Puducherry and Jammu & Kashmir) have it. Statement 4 is incorrect: The Fourth Schedule deals with the allocation of Rajya Sabha seats. So exactly 1 statement(s) are correct.
w: 'Only three' miscounts: exactly 1 statement(s) are correct.
'All four' miscounts: exactly 1 statement(s) are correct.
'None' miscounts: exactly 1 statement(s) are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: The consultative committees of MPs are not treated as parliamentary committees.
Statement-II: A parliamentary committee works under the direction of the Speaker or Chairman, presents its report to the House or the presiding officer, and has a secretariat provided by the Lok Sabha or Rajya Sabha.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct. Statement-II is correct. The consultative committees are excluded precisely because they do not fulfil these conditions, so Statement-II explains Statement-I.
w: Statement-II does supply the reason for Statement-I, so it does explain it.
Statement-II is correct, so it cannot be called incorrect.
Statement-I is correct, so it cannot be called incorrect.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: In a joint sitting of the two Houses the Lok Sabha ordinarily prevails over the Rajya Sabha.
Statement-II: The Lok Sabha has the greater number of members.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct: the Lok Sabha, with the greater number, wins the battle in a joint sitting, except where the combined strength of the ruling party in both Houses is less than that of the opposition parties. Statement-II is correct: the Lok Sabha is the larger House (543 against 245). In a joint sitting votes are counted together, so the larger number is what makes the Lok Sabha prevail; Statement-II explains Statement-I.
w: Statement-II gives the numerical reason for the Lok Sabha's prevailing, so it does explain Statement-I.
Statement-II is correct: the Lok Sabha is the larger House.
Statement-I is correct: the Lok Sabha ordinarily prevails in a joint sitting.
tr: Joint sitting is decided by numbers

questions.q:
Match the entries in List-I with the correct entries in List-II, relating to the special powers of the Rajya Sabha.

List-I
A. Article 249
B. Article 312
C. Article 67
D. Articles 352, 356 and 360

List-II
1. Authorisation of new All-India Services common to the Centre and the States
2. Removal of the Vice-President, which only the Rajya Sabha can initiate
3. A proclamation remaining effective on the approval of the Rajya Sabha alone when the Lok Sabha is dissolved
4. Authorisation of Parliament to make a law on a State List subject
questions.e: Article 249 lets the Rajya Sabha authorise Parliament to legislate on a State List subject (4); Article 312 lets it authorise new All-India Services (1); under Article 67 a resolution to remove the Vice-President can be introduced only in the Rajya Sabha (2); under Articles 352, 356 and 360 a proclamation can stay effective on the Rajya Sabha's approval alone if the Lok Sabha is dissolved (3).
w: Articles 249 and 312 are interchanged: Article 312 concerns All-India Services.
Article 67 and Articles 352, 356, 360 are interchanged: Article 67 concerns the Vice-President's removal.
Article 312 and Article 67 are interchanged: Article 67 concerns the Vice-President's removal.
